title: FLA import: unbounded/decompression-bomb allocations from attacker-controlled sizes (OLE reader + media decode)
description:
Two malformed-input DoS paths in FLA import fixed on the READ/IMPORT side only (write path untouched, owned by 1384/1386).

FIX (1) OLE reader unbounded zero-fill (ole.ts): readStream/readMiniStream now clamp the attacker-controlled 32-bit directory-entry size to the bytes actually reachable via the sector chain (chain.length*sectorSize, capped at file length) / the root mini-stream length. A crafted tiny .fla declaring ~1.5-2GB no longer forces a multi-GB Uint8Array. Also defends the header mini-stream-cutoff-routing vector. Warns on clamp.

FIX (2) media decode bomb (media.ts): decodeLossless rejects bitmaps beyond a pixel budget (either dim >16384 or >16.7Mpx) BEFORE allocating; the lossless inflate now runs into a fixed out buffer sized width*height*4 and the form-d zlib-wrapped path into a 64MiB cap, so a zlib bomb stops at the cap instead of OOMing (verified fflate does not grow a caller-supplied out buffer). GIF-header placeholder path also guarded.

NOTE: flash8-binary.ts:3596 anchor mis-anchor (explicitly 'related low') left untouched to avoid conflict with the write path (1384/1386) and because it is a correctness nit, not a DoS; needs real-fixture validation. Noted as follow-up.

EVIDENCE:
- Full ordered build: pnpm --filter './packages/**' build -> exit 0 (all 8 packages Done).
- pnpm --filter @flash/core test -- --run -> 5634 passed | 8 skipped (346 files).
- New tests: ole.test.ts 'oversized directory-entry size is clamped'; media.test.ts 'decompression-bomb / oversized-allocation guards' (5 cases). All green.
- docs/21-fla-binary-format.md: new section 6.1 'Untrusted input: allocation guards'.
